seo.title: Bhutan Culture and Adventure Tour + Kathmandu | Adventure Access
seo.description: Ten days through Kathmandu and Bhutan: Boudha, Thimphu, Punakha Dzong, a Paro farmhouse and the Tiger's Nest hike. From $3,500.

hero.title: Bhutan Culture and Adventure
hero.subtitle: Kathmandu's Tibetan quarter, then Bhutan's capital, Punakha and the Tiger's Nest
hero.imageAlt: Punakha Dzong across the river below forested hills

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Through Kathmandu, Into Bhutan
paragraphs: Bhutan is a place of old forests, clear rivers, snow-capped peaks and warm, tropical valleys. This Buddhist kingdom is one of the least visited countries in the world, yet it has some of the best hiking, biking, rafting and cultural immersion in the Himalaya.

Bhutan is often best reached through Kathmandu, so this trip uses that time on purpose. Days in Kathmandu's Tibetan quarter add depth to a journey through the Tibetan world on the south side of the Himalaya, before and after Bhutan's history, culture, food and adventure.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Two Capitals and a Kingdom
dayTypes.lede: Kathmandu frames the trip on both ends. In Bhutan, the first days are paced for the altitude, and Punakha is where you can add the adventure you want.

cards.title: Kathmandu days
cards.body: Days 1–3 and 9–10: the Boudha district and its stupa, a meal with your local host, and Thamel's cafes and shops before you fly home.

cards.title: Culture days
cards.body: Days 4–6: a dzong on the way to Thimphu, a walking day in the capital, then Punakha Dzong over Dochu La.

cards.title: Paro and the Tiger's Nest
cards.body: Days 7–8: a farmhouse stay with hot stone baths, and the hike to the Tiger's Nest, reachable only on foot.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: From Boudha to the Tiger's Nest

groups.title: Kathmandu — The Boudha District

image.alt: Boudhanath stupa in Kathmandu strung with prayer flags

prose: Boudha is home to many of Kathmandu's Tibetans, a neighborhood with more signs of Buddhism than Hinduism. Boudhanath Stupa is its cultural center.

days.label: Days 1–3
days.text: Arrive in Kathmandu, where a local guide meets you and hosts you for your time in the city. A private transfer to your hotel in Boudha, time to eat and explore the nearby streets, then an evening meal with your host, who shares what growing up in Nepal and daily life in Kathmandu are like.

groups.overnight: Hotel in the Boudha district, Kathmandu

groups.title: Thimphu — Into the Dragon Kingdom (7,656 ft)

image.alt: Prayer flags above the Thimphu valley

prose: Approaching Bhutan is like nothing else. The Himalaya fill the horizon, and your first Bhutanese hosts are on the plane, since only the national airlines fly in and out. Paro is just the port of entry for now; you will see the best of it at the end.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: Fly to Paro (7,200 ft) and stop for a quick meal. On the way to Thimphu, visit a dzong as a first look at Bhutan's culture and national identity. Check in, rest, then dinner with the group and a full orientation from your guides.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: A walking day in the capital at an acclimatizing pace: a temple complex, a cultural museum and the Takin Preserve, for a first look at Bhutan's Buddhist culture, history and wildlife.

groups.title: Punakha — Over Dochu La to the Dzong
prose: Punakha is an adventurer's dream: hiking, biking, rafting, fishing, fortresses and old myths. Its riverside dzong was built in 1637, saw the coronation of the first king in 1907, and was the capital until 1955.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: Over Dochu La, with views of Bhutan's great peaks from the top, then down to Punakha. Wander the dzong while your guide explains its many roles. This is the place to extend the trip if you want more time on an activity.

groups.title: Paro — Farmhouse and the Tiger's Nest

image.alt: The Tiger's Nest monastery on its cliff

prose: Back to where it began. A family farmhouse, some dating back seven or more generations, is home in Paro, with homegrown food and a hot stone bath. The Tiger's Nest can only be reached on foot, and the hike is the best way to end any trip to Bhutan.

days.label: Days 7–8
days.text: Walk Paro's streets, try Bhutan's homegrown coffee and shop for something to remember the trip by. Hike to the Tiger's Nest, then reward yourself with another hot stone bath.

image.alt: A snow peak rising above the clouds

days.label: Day 9
days.text: A morning flight back to Kathmandu and on to Thamel, a busy district of cafes, restaurants and shops popular with Nepal's adventurers. Lunch with your local host, time to repack at the hotel, and a final meal together.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: A private transfer to Kathmandu airport for your onward flight.

pullQuote: Approaching Bhutan is like nothing else.

highlights.title: The Tiger's Nest
highlights.body: One of Bhutan's most iconic places, reachable only on foot. The hike combines activity, culture and mountainside forest in one day.
highlights.imageAlt: The Tiger's Nest monastery on its cliff

highlights.title: Punakha Dzong
highlights.body: Built in 1637, site of the first king's coronation in 1907 and Bhutan's capital until 1955.

highlights.title: Boudha and Your Local Host
highlights.body: The Tibetan heart of Kathmandu around Boudhanath Stupa, and an evening hearing your host's story of growing up in Nepal.
highlights.imageAlt: Boudhanath stupa in Kathmandu strung with prayer flags

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Getting there
cards.body: The trip starts and ends in Kathmandu. Flights between Kathmandu and Paro are included; flights to and from Kathmandu are not.

cards.title: Visas
cards.body: Your Bhutan visa is included. Nepal visas are not, and are paid on arrival.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Paro sits at 7,200 feet and Thimphu at 7,656 feet. The first days in Bhutan are paced to help you adjust.

cards.title: Your guides
cards.body: Professional English-speaking guides travel with you, with English-speaking guides for each activity, and a local host in Kathmandu.

cards.title: Hot stone baths
cards.body: A Bhutanese tradition common in Paro's farmhouses, and a highlight for any trip to Bhutan.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: City Hotels and a Farmhouse
paragraphs: In Kathmandu you stay in the Boudha district. Our preferred packages in Bhutan use 3–5 star hotels, and in Paro a family farmhouse. Farmhouses are not rated like hotels, but every guest names them as a highlight.

included: Professional English-speaking guides and activity guides
Activities as listed in your itinerary
Regional flights between Kathmandu and Paro
Accommodations: 3–5 star hotels in Bhutan and a farmhouse stay
All meals in Kathmandu and Bhutan
All ground transportation by private vehicle
excluded: Alcohol (we strongly encourage little or none while acclimatizing)
Tips for guides (we will explain local tipping customs)
Personal clothing and equipment (we send a packing list)
